stemMd: For an endothermic forward reaction at equilibrium, increasing temperature generally favours which direction?

options.label: B
options.textMd: Neither direction because temperature never affects equilibrium

options.label: C
options.textMd: A direction determined solely by the vessel's colour

options.label: D
options.textMd: The reverse direction because all heating favours reactants

options.label: E
options.textMd: Only complete disappearance of every molecule

explanationMd: Treat heat as required by the endothermic direction. Raising temperature favours the direction that absorbs it; unlike adding a catalyst, temperature can alter the equilibrium constant.

distractorRationale.c: Vessel colour is not the thermodynamic criterion.
distractorRationale.d: The direction depends on reaction enthalpy.
distractorRationale.e: Equilibrium shifts do not destroy matter.
distractorRationale.b: Temperature can change the equilibrium constant.
